args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (unhealthy, error rate 18% across us-east, us-west, eu-west). Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Rolled back checkout-api in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rollback reported rolled_out/verified in all regions. Follow-up: root-cause v2.3.1 before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident for it.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks, and 18% of requests were returning errors.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions. A follow-up check shows the service is healthy, with the error rate down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2) is open, and the on-call engineer has been paged. It describes the failure, the rollback and the follow-up work.

The release-candidate build of v2.3.1 (v2.3.1-rc) also failed health checks in staging, so the problem was visible before it reached production. v2.3.1 shouldn't be deployed again until the root cause is found.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
